selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The FEHB Protection Act of 2025 requires the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to establish new verification rules, conduct family eligibility audits, assess fraud risks, and implement removal procedures for ineligible individuals enrolled in Federal Employees Health Benefits plans. It also provides dedicated funding from health contributions for oversight, audit activities, and administrative system maintenance from fiscal year 2026 onwards.

affected_groups.effect: Must undergo stricter verification processes when adding family members and will be subject to a comprehensive eligibility audit requiring documents like marriage and birth certificates, with potential removal if found ineligible.
affected_groups.group: Enrollees in the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with issuing new verification regulations, creating disenrollment processes, conducting a multi-year audit, and managing dedicated oversight funding.
Required to coordinate with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to conduct the comprehensive family member eligibility audit.

key_provisions: Requires the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to issue regulations and implement a process to verify qualifying life events and family member eligibility when adding members during open season or other times.
Mandates that fraud risk assessments for the program include evaluations of individuals who are enrolled or covered despite not being eligible.

Requires a comprehensive family member eligibility verification audit over a three-year period, beginning one year after enactment, using marriage certificates, birth certificates, and other documents.
Directs the development of a process to disenroll or remove ineligible individuals within six months of the bill's enactment.

Provides specific annual funding caps from contributions for the Office of Personnel Management to develop, maintain, and oversee enrollment and eligibility systems, ranging from $36,792,000 in FY 2026 to $58,556,117 in FY 2033, with subsequent annual 2.2 percent increases.
Allocates $80,000,000 in fiscal year 2026 from contributions for the family member audit, allowing fund transfers to employing offices as needed.

Establishes dedicated funding limits for the Office of Personnel Management Office of the Inspector General to conduct oversight activities, starting at $5,090,278 in FY 2026 with 2.2 percent annual increases thereafter.
missing_information: The total number of federal employees and family members currently enrolled in the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program who will be affected.
The estimated number of currently ineligible individuals improperly receiving coverage under the program.
The broader economic impact on health insurance premiums resulting from removing ineligible participants.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The FEHB Protection Act of 2025 requires the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to establish new verification rules, conduct family eligibility audits, assess fraud risks, and implement removal procedures for ineligible individuals enrolled in Federal Employees Health Benefits plans. It also provides dedicated funding from health contributions for oversight, audit activities, and administrative system maintenance from fiscal year 2026 onwards.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes formal, mandatory auditing and verification frameworks for federal employee health plans to prevent ineligible individuals from receiving coverage, backed by tens of millions of dollars in dedicated annual funding for administrative oversight and audits.
